question: A 13-year-old girl discloses to you during consultation that she has been sexually abused by a neighbour. Her mother is present and begs you not to report, fearing social stigma. Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act 2012?

answers.text: Respect the mother's wishes and maintain confidentiality, as parental consent overrides mandatory reporting for a child over 12 years.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Parental wishes do not override mandatory reporting under POCSO. The Act applies to all persons under 18 years and Section 19 imposes a mandatory duty to report on any person with knowledge of an offence — including doctors — regardless of parental consent.

answers.text: File a report to the local police or Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) as required by Section 19 of the POCSO Act 2012, irrespective of the mother's objection.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Under Section 19 of the POCSO Act 2012, any person (including a healthcare professional) who has knowledge that a child (defined as anyone under 18 years) has been subjected to a sexual offence is legally obligated to report it to the police or SJPU immediately. Failure to do so is itself a punishable offence under Section 21.

answers.text: Defer reporting and first obtain a written consent from the child, since she is 13 and capable of giving assent for medicolegal proceedings.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Mandatory reporting under POCSO Section 19 does not require the child's assent or the family's consent. The obligation is triggered by the knowledge of the offence, not by a request from the child or family.

answers.text: Refer the family to a child welfare NGO and allow them to decide whether to report, as the doctor's responsibility is limited to medical management.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The legal duty to report under POCSO Section 19 rests directly on the doctor who has knowledge of the offence. Delegating this to the family or a third party does not discharge the doctor's statutory obligation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the POCSO Act 2012: Section 19 imposes a mandatory, unconditional reporting duty on anyone — including doctors — who has knowledge of a sexual offence against a child under 18 years. Failure to report is itself an offence under Section 21.

Well done. POCSO 2012 Section 19 mandates immediate reporting by any person with knowledge of a sexual offence against a child (<18 years). This duty is non-negotiable and supersedes parental or patient confidentiality concerns.
